description: PROPOSED, NOT NORMATIVE (RFC-010, Draft). The muscle names every FDS application would share, so a user's training history moves between applications without translation. An entry is either a muscle (a muscle or a named part of one) or a group that rolls up other entries. atlasAreas are informative hints naming areas of the VITNESS production body atlas (vulovix/body-muscles, Apache-2.0); they do not constrain any FDS document.

entries.label: Abductors
entries.description: The hip abductors, which move the thigh away from the midline. Rolls up the gluteus medius, the only abductor this list names on its own.

entries.label: Abs
entries.description: The abdominal wall at the front of the trunk, as most people use the word. Rolls up the rectus abdominis.

entries.label: Adductors
entries.description: The inner-thigh muscles that draw the thigh toward the midline.

entries.label: Anterior Deltoid
entries.description: The front head of the deltoid. Raises the arm forward and helps in pressing.

entries.label: Back
entries.description: The whole back of the trunk, from the upper trapezius to the lower back.

entries.label: Biceps
entries.description: The front of the upper arm, as most people use the word. Rolls up the biceps brachii.

entries.label: Biceps brachii
entries.description: The two-headed muscle at the front of the upper arm. Bends the elbow and turns the palm up.

entries.label: Biceps femoris
entries.description: The outer hamstring. Bends the knee and extends the hip.

entries.label: Brachialis
entries.description: The muscle under the biceps that bends the elbow whatever the grip.

entries.label: Brachioradialis
entries.description: The forearm muscle on the thumb side that bends the elbow, strongest with a neutral grip.

entries.label: Calves
entries.description: The back of the lower leg.

entries.label: Chest
entries.description: The pectoral muscles at the front of the chest.

entries.label: Deltoid
entries.description: The shoulder's cap muscle, made of three heads.

entries.label: Erector Spinae
entries.description: The long muscles either side of the spine that extend and hold it upright.

entries.label: Forearms
entries.description: The muscles between the elbow and the wrist.

entries.label: Full Body
entries.description: The whole body. For work that loads no particular group more than the rest.

entries.label: Gastrocnemius
entries.description: The two-headed surface calf muscle. Points the foot and helps bend the knee.

entries.label: Glutes
entries.description: The buttock muscles.

entries.label: Gluteus Maximus
entries.description: The largest buttock muscle. Extends the hip.

entries.label: Gluteus Medius
entries.description: The buttock muscle on the side of the hip. Abducts the hip and steadies the pelvis on one leg.

entries.label: Hamstrings
entries.description: The back of the thigh.

entries.label: Hip Flexors
entries.description: The muscles at the front of the hip that lift the thigh toward the trunk.

entries.label: Inner Pecs
entries.description: The inner portion of the pectoralis major, beside the sternum.

entries.label: Lateral Deltoid
entries.description: The side head of the deltoid. Raises the arm out to the side.

entries.label: Lats
entries.description: The latissimus dorsi, the broad muscle of the mid and lower back. Pulls the arm down and back.

entries.label: Legs
entries.description: Everything from the hips down.

entries.label: Lower Back
entries.description: The lumbar region of the back.

entries.label: Lower Pecs
entries.description: The lower portion of the pectoralis major.

entries.label: Lower Trapezius
entries.description: The lower fibres of the trapezius. Draws the shoulder blade down.

entries.label: Middle Back
entries.description: The region between the shoulder blades.

entries.label: Middle Trapezius
entries.description: The middle fibres of the trapezius. Draws the shoulder blades together.

entries.label: Neck
entries.description: The muscles of the neck, front and back.

entries.label: Obliques
entries.description: The muscles on the sides of the abdomen that rotate and side-bend the trunk.

entries.label: Posterior Deltoid
entries.description: The rear head of the deltoid. Draws the arm back.

entries.label: Quadratus Lumborum
entries.description: The deep lower-back muscle between the ribs and the pelvis. Side-bends the trunk and steadies the pelvis.

entries.label: Quadriceps
entries.description: The four-headed muscle at the front of the thigh. Extends the knee.

entries.label: Rectus Abdominis
entries.description: The vertical muscle at the front of the abdomen. Flexes the trunk.

entries.label: Serratus
entries.description: The serratus anterior, on the side of the ribcage. Holds the shoulder blade against the ribs and moves it forward.

entries.label: Shoulders
entries.description: The shoulder region, as most people use the word.

entries.label: Soleus
entries.description: The flat calf muscle under the gastrocnemius. Points the foot, and works most with the knee bent.

entries.label: Tibialis Anterior
entries.description: The muscle at the front of the shin that lifts the foot.

entries.label: Traps
entries.description: The trapezius, the large muscle from the neck across the upper back.

entries.label: Triceps
entries.description: The back of the upper arm, made of three heads.

entries.label: Triceps Lateral Head
entries.description: The outer head of the triceps.

entries.label: Triceps Long Head
entries.description: The head of the triceps that crosses the shoulder.

entries.label: Triceps Medial Head
entries.description: The deep head of the triceps, closest to the bone.

entries.label: Upper Back
entries.description: The upper back: the rear shoulder, the upper lats and the trapezius below the neck.

entries.label: Upper Pecs
entries.description: The upper (clavicular) portion of the pectoralis major.

entries.label: Upper Trapezius
entries.description: The upper fibres of the trapezius. Shrugs the shoulders.

entries.label: Wrist Extensors
entries.description: The muscles on the back of the forearm that extend the wrist.

entries.label: Wrist Flexors
entries.description: The muscles on the palm side of the forearm that flex the wrist.
